faq: Will limits block my real customers?
Limits are set with you using your normal traffic as a guide, so regular use stays well under them. Customers who hit a limit get a clear message that says when to retry.
Which log tool will you use?
We use what you already have, such as your host's log viewer, Datadog, Logtail or a simple database table. If you have nothing, we recommend a low-cost option and set it up.
Do the logs store customer data?
We keep personal and sensitive values out of logs by default, such as passwords, tokens and card details. We tell you what is recorded so it fits your privacy policy.
Can you do this for an API you did not build?
Yes, if we can add code or a gateway in front of it. Add us to your project and we check the setup first, then confirm the scope in writing.

desc:
API rate limiting and request logging setup keeps one busy caller from slowing everyone down and lets you see what happened when a call fails. Ecom Swift LLC adds fair usage limits, trace IDs and readable logs to your API.

## What is API rate limiting?

API rate limiting caps how many requests a caller can send in a set period. When someone goes over the cap, the API replies with a clear "too many requests" message instead of trying to serve every call. Limits can apply to the whole API, to each key or to each route.

Request logging is the partner of limiting. It writes down each call with its time, route, status and a trace ID, so you can follow a single request from start to finish.

## What happens without limits and logs

An unlimited API depends on everyone behaving. A partner script with a loop bug, a scraper or a retry storm can send thousands of requests in a minute. The servers slow down, and the customers who did nothing wrong feel the effect.

Without logs, you cannot even tell who caused it. A customer reports an error, and your team has nothing to search. Guessing takes hours, and the same fault comes back.

## How limits and logs improve the service

Limits protect the many from the few. Because each key has its own allowance, a runaway client hits its own ceiling and the rest of your users see no change. Usage plans also let you offer different allowances to different customers, which can support a clear product offer.

Logs shorten every investigation. A trace ID tells you exactly which calls belonged to a failed order, and a searchable log view shows the pattern behind a spike in errors. Support answers faster, developers fix faster and slow routes become visible before customers complain.

## What a sound setup includes

- A global limit as a safety net for the whole API.
- Limits per key and per route where fair use differs.
- A simple set of usage plans for different kinds of customers.
- A clear message and a retry hint when a limit is reached.
- A log entry for every request with time, route, status and duration.
- A trace ID returned to the caller and written in the log.
- Sensitive data, such as passwords, card details and tokens, kept out of logs.
- A searchable view in your log tool, plus a short guide for tracing a failed call.
- Retention rules, so logs do not fill your storage or your budget.

## How we set it up

We read how your API is used today and talk with you about who the callers are. Then we choose sensible limits, add them in front of your routes and test that normal use passes while excess use is stopped politely. The same pass adds the logging, with a careful review of what must never be recorded.

The Basic package adds one global limit and a simple log. Standard adds limits per key and route, usage plans, trace IDs and a searchable log. Premium adds daily usage counts, alerts when errors spike, retention rules and a report of slow requests. Final numbers depend on your servers and customers, so we tune them with you.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with generous limits and tighten them from real usage.
- Tell developers about limits in your docs.
- Return a clear message and a hint for when to retry.
- Mask or leave out personal and secret values in logs.
- Review the slowest routes regularly.

**Avoid:**
- Setting one tiny limit for every caller.
- Blocking requests with no explanation.
- Logging full request bodies that contain private data.
- Keeping logs forever with no plan for storage.
- Forgetting to tell your own team where the logs are.

## Who it is for

A company opening its API to partners wants protection before the first heavy user arrives. A team that fought a mysterious slowdown needs logs to find the cause. A product that plans paid tiers needs usage plans with different allowances.

## What we need from you

Share where the API runs, which framework or gateway it uses and any log tool you already pay for. We need developer or collaborator access to the code and hosting, never passwords. A sample of typical traffic helps us choose first limits.
